end of button, Mario Silva's avatar Mario Silva $22M FA @marios Jan 14 Apple could have signed a life-changing deal with Gemini! I think that most investors are already aware of this deal, but most people are still not aware of how this deal can change $AAPL Apple's AI failures in the last years to develop an AI model that fits perfectly with its core values. Most analysts were bashing Apple in the last years because it was not able to go at the same pace as the AI developments built by the other M7. There was a big reason why the AI requirements for Apple were way more challenging than those of the other big techs. The reason is that Cook did not want to train the data in external data centers, where the user's data stop being private, to be a tool that is used for those big techs. As such, Cook wanted each Apple device to train the data for AI "on-device" without the need of external data centers. If a user requires more AI capacity, Apple offers the Private Cloud Computing (PCC), where the user's data will be deleted as soon as it is used. Maybe you are thinking, "Why does Apple care about the privacy and security of the user's data?" Well, to understand it, we need to review which were the core principles developed by Tim Cook since he took over as CEO in 2011. Indeed, since Tim Cook took over as CEO of Apple in 2011, he has set six pillars over which his leadership will thrive in the next few years. I took this information from the book Tim Cook: The Genius Who Took Apple to the Next Level, written by Leander Kahney: Accessibility: Apple considers accessibility a fundamental human right, and technology should be accessible to everybody in the world. Education: Apple considers education a fundamental human right, and high-quality education should be available for everybody in the world. Inclusion and Diversity: Apple considers that diverse teams are what make innovation possible. Environment: Apple boosts environmental responsibility in the design and manufacturing of its products. Privacy and Security: Apple considers privacy a fundamental human right. Every Apple product is designed from scratch to protect the privacy and security of each user. Responsibility of suppliers: Apple educates and empowers its different suppliers within its supply chain while helping in the conservation of the most precious environmental resources. These foundations have been the pillars over which Apple has delivered over 1800% of stock appreciation since Cook started as CEO in 2011. Now, maybe you still have many doubts about why privacy and security are very important for users, particularly in AI. Nobody is paying attention now to this important matter, but the other big techs are gaining a lot of power using their users' data freely, and there are no boundaries to how they are using them. Sooner or later, this will be an issue that these big techs will need to tackle if the government and regulators decide to act to protect users. So, Apple does not want to be caught off guard, and it's the first one working hard since the very beginning to develop an AI that fits with this core pillar: the privacy and security of the user's data. It was in this particular context, when Apple had already exhausted its own possibilities to develop this kind of AI model for itself, that a new and complex agreement was signed with Alphabet to provide a suitable AI development that fulfills Apple's requirements. Some interesting points about the agreement in which Apple will have to pay USD 1 billion to Google: 1. It's a "White Label" Deal (Apple Runs the Brain) Contrary to how most people use AI (sending data to a company like OpenAI or Google), Apple isn't "sending" you to Google. The "Weight" Transfer: Apple has essentially licensed the "model weights" (the brain) of Gemini. The Private Cloud: Instead of running Gemini in Google’s data centers, Apple is running a custom, "sanitized" version of Gemini on its own Private Cloud Compute (PCC). This uses Apple’s own custom silicon (M-series chips) that are physically designed to be "stateless"—meaning they process your request and then "forget" everything instantly. 2. Why Gemini over OpenAI or Grok? While OpenAI was Apple's first partner, several factors made Gemini the "foundational" choice for the 2026 Siri overhaul: Multimodal Efficiency: Gemini (specifically the "Flash" and "Nano" versions) was built from the ground up to handle text, images, and video simultaneously. This is critical for features like "Visual Intelligence" (where you point your camera at a restaurant and Siri tells you the menu). The "Nano" Advantage: Google developed Gemini Nano, which is currently the gold standard for high-performance AI that can fit entirely on a phone's chip. While OpenAI's models are powerful, they are often too "heavy" to run locally without a massive battery drain. Infrastructure Stability: Apple needs a partner that can handle 1.5 billion Siri requests a day. Google’s global infrastructure and deep integration with Apple (via the existing search deal) made them a more stable "plumbing" partner than the smaller, more volatile OpenAI. 3. The "On-Device" Priority I mentioned Apple’s goal of operating without data centers. They have achieved this through a three-tier system: On-Device (Apple’s Models): Simple tasks (summarizing a text, editing a photo) happen 100% on your iPhone. Neither Google nor Apple ever sees this data. Private Cloud (Gemini on Apple Silicon): For harder tasks, the data goes to Apple’s secure servers. This is where the Gemini "brain" lives, but it is blindfolded. It sees the data, processes it, and deletes it. External (Optional ChatGPT): For general knowledge questions ("How do I fix a leaky pipe?"), Siri will ask if you want to use ChatGPT. This is the only time data leaves Apple's secure "bubble," and you have to give explicit permission. 4. Verification: The "Sealed Box" The most "Apple-like" part of this deal is that Apple has made the Gemini-PCC environment auditable. Independent Oversight: Independent security researchers can actually inspect the code running on Apple’s AI servers to verify that the data is being deleted and that Google isn't secretly "training" on it. The "Privacy Shield": Because Apple controls the hardware (the server chips), they can guarantee that no persistent storage exists on the AI processing units. As of January 12, 2026, Apple essentially admitted that building a world-class AI from scratch while maintaining their "Privacy First" requirements was a mountain too high to climb alone. By signing this multi-year deal to use Gemini 3 as the "Foundation" for Apple Intelligence, they have effectively "outsourced the brain" to catch up in months what would have taken years. I am holding Apple stock at 121 dollars per share which give me a lot of margin of safety, but I am very positive with this deal which, in the end, is no different from other deals Apple has made in the past, outsourcing products and services to focus on what matters to Apple. "Outsource products and services in particular specialties, and Apple focuses on what matters to it." 45 Comments $134M, not pressed
The secret behind F1’s massive boom
link, The secret behind F1’s massive boom
heading, The secret behind F1’s massive boom, level 3

A legend in the world of autosport, from an executive standpoint. That’s where we find Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali. After rising through the financial and sporting ranks at Ferrari, he served as their Team Principal from 2008 to 2014, notably leading the Scuderia to a Constructors' Championship in 2008. Following a transformative stint as CEO of Lamborghini, where he oversaw the successful launch of the Urus SUV, he took the reins as CEO of Formula 1 in 2021. In his current role, Domenicali has been the chief architect of F1’s global expansion, successfully navigating the sport into a record-breaking 24-race calendar and spearheading the massive 2026 technical regulations reset. Domenicali drove up to the Opening Bid Unfiltered podcast mic with Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to chat about the surging sport that is Formula 1. The F1 brand has gotten a huge lift from the successful Netflix show ‘Drive to Survive and ever increasing amounts of Corporate America sponsorships. With seemingly all eyes on the sport – especially now with Cadillac added to the grid – Domenicali has his work cut out for him to keep the growth as hot as Lewis Hamilton lap time.
end of link, The secret behind F1’s massive boom

end of button, Mario Silva's avatar Mario Silva $22M FA @marios Feb 27 Apple vs. The M6: Why the "Growth" Narrative is a Mathematical Trap I’ve watched investors dump Apple $AAPL lately to chase the "Magnificent 6" euphoria. They’ve fallen for a simple narrative: "Apple doesn't grow anymore." But after diving into the 10-Ks of the entire group, I’ve found that Apple is a fundamentally different beast that deserves to be a core position in any portfolio. The NVIDIA "Microbe" vs. Reality Most investors are obsessed with revenue. NVIDIA $NVDA is the current star, with a staggering 73% average revenue growth over the last five years. But as a long-term investor, I think of Warren Buffett’s famous "microbe" warning. Buffett often cites the Law of Large Numbers to explain that exponential growth eventually hits a wall. If a microbe doubles every minute, it looks like it has infinite space until the very last moments before the bottle is full. Buffett’s core principle is clear: "The law of large numbers eventually takes over. You can’t grow a business to the point where it exceeds the size of the world's economy." NVIDIA is no longer a small microbe; at its current scale, maintaining that 73% growth is mathematically impossible because it would eventually outpace the global GDP itself. The Tim Cook "Asset-Light" Masterclass While the rest of the M6 are burning billions in an infrastructure war, Apple is playing the game Tim Cook perfected: "Own the intellectual property, not the assets." Cook famously views inventory as "fundamentally evil"—comparing it to milk that goes bad. By outsourcing manufacturing but "insourcing" the design of its own silicon, Apple creates value in a way the others can't match. My analysis of the 10-Ks reveals why Apple is a "Quality" outlier: The Buyback King: Apple is the only M6 company that consistently uses more than 80% of its FCF for share buybacks. Capital Efficiency: Despite being a hardware giant, Apple’s R&D expenses consume the least amount of its Gross Margins compared to its peers. Return on Capital: Apple generates the highest ROE and ROIC for every dollar invested back into the business. Conclusion: A Luxury Brand in a Tech Wrapper Microsoft $MSFT, Amazon $AMZN, and Google $GOOG have "utility" moats—they are useful until they aren't. Apple has an identity moat. It is a Veblen Good where the brand itself is the value. While the others fight over who has the fastest chip, Apple is simply waiting to turn the "smartest AI" into a premium feature for its loyal ecosystem. As Tim Cook says: "Do not trade your Apple stock, just hold it." 15 Comments $88M, not pressed

Privacy and Security: Apple considers privacy a fundamental human right. Every Apple product is designed from scratch to protect the privacy and security of each user. Responsibility of suppliers: Apple educates and empowers its different suppliers within its supply chain while helping in the conservation of the most precious environmental resources. These foundations have been the pillars over which Apple has delivered over 1800% of stock appreciation since Cook started as CEO in 2011. Now, maybe you still have many doubts about why privacy and security are very important for users, particularly in AI. Nobody is paying attention now to this important matter, but the other big techs are gaining a lot of power using their users' data freely, and there are no boundaries to how they are using them. Sooner or later, this will be an issue that these big techs will need to tackle if the government and regulators decide to act to protect users. So, Apple does not want to be caught off guard, and it's the first one working hard since the very beginning to develop an AI that fits with this core pillar: the privacy and security of the user's data. It was in this particular context, when Apple had already exhausted its own possibilities to develop this kind of AI model for itself, that a new and complex agreement was signed with Alphabet to provide a suitable AI development that fulfills Apple's requirements. Some interesting points about the agreement in which Apple will have to pay USD 1 billion to Google: 1. It's a "White Label" Deal (Apple Runs the Brain) Contrary to how most people use AI (sending data to a company like OpenAI or Google), Apple isn't "sending" you to Google. The "Weight" Transfer: Apple has essentially licensed the "model weights" (the brain) of Gemini. The Private Cloud: Instead of running Gemini in Google’s data centers, Apple is running a custom, "sanitized" version of Gemini on its own Private Cloud Compute (PCC). This uses Apple’s own custom silicon (M-series chips) that are physically designed to be "stateless"—meaning they process your request and then "forget" everything instantly. 2. Why Gemini over OpenAI or Grok? While OpenAI was Apple's first partner, several factors made Gemini the "foundational" choice for the 2026 Siri overhaul: Multimodal Efficiency: Gemini (specifically the "Flash" and "Nano" versions) was built from the ground up to handle text, images, and video simultaneously. This is critical for features like "Visual Intelligence" (where you point your camera at a restaurant and Siri tells you the menu). The "Nano" Advantage: Google developed Gemini Nano, which is currently the gold standard for high-performance AI that can fit entirely on a phone's chip. While OpenAI's models are powerful, they are often too "heavy" to run locally without a massive battery drain. Infrastructure Stability: Apple needs a partner that can handle 1.5 billion Siri requests a day. Google’s global infrastructure and deep integration with Apple (via the existing search deal) made them a more stable "plumbing" partner than the smaller, more volatile OpenAI. 3. The "On-Device" Priority I mentioned Apple’s goal of operating without data centers. They have achieved this through a three-tier system: On-Device (Apple’s Models): Simple tasks (summarizing a text, editing a photo) happen 100% on your iPhone. This is where the Gemini "brain" lives, but it is blindfolded. It sees the data, processes it, and deletes it. External (Optional ChatGPT): For general knowledge questions ("How do I fix a leaky pipe?"), Siri will ask if you want to use ChatGPT. This is the only time data leaves Apple's secure "bubble," and you have to give explicit permission. 4. Verification: The "Sealed Box" The most "Apple-like" part of this deal is that Apple has made the Gemini-PCC environment auditable. Independent Oversight: Independent security researchers can actually inspect the code running on Apple’s AI servers to verify that the data is being deleted and that Google isn't secretly "training" on it. The "Privacy Shield": Because Apple controls the hardware (the server chips), they can guarantee that no persistent storage exists on the AI processing units. As of January 12, 2026, Apple essentially admitted that building a world-class AI from scratch while maintaining their "Privacy First" requirements was a mountain too high to climb alone. By signing this multi-year deal to use Gemini 3 as the "Foundation" for Apple Intelligence, they have effectively "outsourced the brain" to catch up in months what would have taken years. I am holding Apple stock at 121 dollars per share which give me a lot of margin of safety, but I am very positive with this deal which, in the end, is no different from other deals Apple has made in the past, outsourcing products and services to focus on what matters to Apple. "Outsource products and services in particular specialties, and Apple focuses on what matters to it." 45 Comments $134M, not pressed
